content:
oncall-bot: Incident alert: p99 latency spike detected for inference.gateway (region: eu-west-1). Alert threshold breached at 14:02 UTC. Affected customers: several hosted API keys seeing streaming stalls.

sara: seeing p95 ~600ms -> 1.8s, p99 jumping to 6s for streaming responses. spike started ~14:00. dashboards show config-fetch latency and auth token store errors around same time.

mike: copying graphs: auth-store.latency.p95 = 1200ms, config-fetch.latency.p95 = 900ms, db-connections > 90% in pool.

julia: is this the same tokenstore cluster that had an upgrade earlier? I saw a deploy in eu-west-1 at 13:45 from deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-15T13:44:21Z -> service/tokenstore:v3.2.0 rolled to eu-west-1 (canary->50%).

charles: ok, probable correlation. Tokenstore errors show: 
```
ERROR auth.tokenstore.get token_fetch_timeout: context deadline exceeded (deadline=1000ms)
WARN auth.tokenstore.retry count=3 last_err="connection reset by peer"
```

infra-sre: from infra metrics: connection resets on tokenstore-backend-2 ~13:47 and then backoff. Also config-store calls to controlplane flagged feature-eval are waiting on token fetch.

sara: customer-facing impact: streaming tails are stalling (client connections stay open but no tokens forwarded). A few 5xxs logged when fallback fails. Need live mitigation ASAP.

mike: mitigation options: 1) increase auth token cache TTL and enable local cache path for gateway (fast) 2) rollback tokenstore deploy (slower but safer) 3) route new streaming traffic to eu-central region (cross-region adds lat but may reduce failures)

julia: +1 for enabling local cache first (non-disruptive). Where's the toggle?

charles: config flag exists: `gateway.auth.local_cache.enabled` default false. We can flip for region eu-west-1 via console feature flags API. Patchable at runtime.

infra-sre: note: feature flag eval currently depends on config-fetch service which is also showing elevated p99 due to calls to feature-eval which query tokenstore for service identity. So flipping flag might still hit control plane unless we patch the gateway to short-circuit.

sara: can we deploy a hotfix to gateway to short-circuit auth token validation (only for internal tokens) while we stabilize? Need risk assessment.

mike: hotfix path: small change to bypass tokenstore when `X-Internal-Bypass: true` header present and origin is internal LB. Quick canary then roll. But that requires deploy (~15-20 min). Local cache flip ~2 min if it doesn't call control plane.

julia: I'll try the console flip first: `curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood/flags/gateway.auth.local_cache.enabled -d '{"regions": ["eu-west-1"], "value": true}'` (pseudo).

charles: before flipping, add temporary increase to tokenstore connection pool and lower timeouts to avoid context deadlines. But that's config on tokenstore hosts; infra-sre can run a scaling action.

infra-sre: scaling up tokenstore replicas by +2 in eu-west-1 now. Command: `k scale deployment tokenstore -n services --replicas=5 --context=eu-west-1` (executed). Watching.

oncall-bot: oncall handoff reminder: @mike is primary until 15:00 UTC, then @julia takes over. Marking pager state: investigating.

sara: started customer impact log for PG: 
- start: 2026-03-15T14:00:12Z 
- symptom: streaming stalls / long-first-byte / p99 token delays
- affected: hosted api keys in eu-west-1, ~2% of total requests
- mitigation steps: scaling tokenstore, toggling local cache, consider rollback

mike: tokenstore replicas are not yet healthy: new pods crash with `panic: failed to open DB file: resource temporarily unavailable` — looks like underlying disk i/o contention on backend storage.

charles: that points to DB control-plane dependency. Tokenstore uses embedded leveldb on attached disk. If the AZ had transient storage pressure, scaling won't help until root cause cleared.

julia: can we set gateway to gracefully fallback: if tokenstore errors, use short-lived unsigned tokens for streaming ingress verification (conservative) so sessions continue while we solve persistence?

sara: need to coordinate with security/product — that changes trust model. Quick temporary policy: allow existing active sessions to continue but block new long-lived sessions above threshold.

mike: I've opened an emergency PR for gateway hotfix: bypass token validation for requests with active session cookie present and signature verified by local public key (no tokenstore call). Testing in canary now (gw-canary-3).

infra-sre: controlplane logs show a spike in config-fetch fanout at 13:59: `fanout_count=12000` — looks like a config-sync storm possibly triggered by feature-flag rollout. That increased writes to tokenstore DB because each config fetch triggers identity verification.

charles: do we have the rollout id? deploy-bot mentioned feature flags earlier — but I didn't see a feature rollout. Could be client-side re-eval loop.

julia: I see repeated calls from a small set of gateways: `gateway-12x` with `retry=exponential` and tight backoff. Might be a bad client library change causing retries.

sara: customer comms: drafting a short status message: "We’re investigating elevated streaming latency in eu-west-1. Some requests may stall; mitigation in progress. No data loss expected." Want to send at 14:12.

mike: gateway canary hotfix passed smoke tests. Rolling to 30% -> 60% now. If that holds, it'll stop new tokenstore calls for active sessions.

infra-sre: disk i/o metrics improving after moving some IO off hot node and restarting underlying storage: iops from 4500 -> 900. new tokenstore pods now healthy.

oncall-bot: Incident update posted to status page: https://status.redwood/incident/2469123456 (draft).

charles: metrics now: p95 down to ~400ms, p99 down to ~1.4s. Streaming stalls reduced by ~70%. Still seeing sporadic tail spikes from requests that hit aged config entries.

julia: recommend keeping gateway hotfix and local cache on for at least 2 hours, then rollback to normal flow after full stabilization and postmortem. Also run a config-store audit to find the source of the config-fetch fanout.

sara: assigning follow-ups: 
- infra-sre: postmortem for tokenstore storage saturation (assign)
- eng-platform (charles/mike): audit gateway client retry behavior and fix library if needed
- product/sec: review temporary bypass policy and approve/deny (julia to coordinate)
- support: list affected customers and provide targeted notice if they ask (sara)

mike: I'll also prepare a canary rollback plan if any regression appears.

julia: handing off to @mike at 14:30 for next steps. I'll stay on the thread until 15:00.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: julia -> mike at 14:30 UTC.

sara: end-of-thread note for handoff: we achieved partial mitigation by: scaling tokenstore, applying gateway local cache bypass, and rolling a hotfix to short-circuit tokenstore lookups for active sessions. Root cause: storage IO contention causing tokenstore DB failures amplified by config-fetch fanout from a retry storm. Postmortem owners assigned.

charles: leaving some logs for postmortem: `config-fetch: caller=gateway-12x retries=8 fanout=12000`, `tokenstore: db_open_err=resource temporarily unavailable`, `gateway: token_fetch_latency_ms=6500`.

mike: will keep monitoring p99 and streaming success rate. if anyone sees regression ping pager. :thumbsup: 

oncall-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident closed to active paging at 15:05 UTC if no regressions.
